title: Can anyone help a little?
author: No_Effective8213
selftext:
I personally enjoy playing the visual novel games that are made with AI if they are done right and the story is not lacking.

It's been a dream of mine to make a visual novel and I can code but am shit at art. 

Using AI to generate the art would be the only way for me but I don't know how to generate different characters with consistent design and world map in the same art style of my choosing.

Can anyone guide me please?

comments.author: the_builder_ai
comments.body:
I’m work on games using AI-generated art, so I’ve run into this quite a bit. The biggest thing is to build a set of references first, then reuse those throughout. For characters, I’d start with an approved character design by getting a clear portrait and full-body image you like before making additional expressions or poses. Then a short design description that specifies the hairstyle, eye color, outfit, accessories, and proportions. Keep those details consistent in your prompts. Use the same reference image for each new generation: Ask for that specific character with a different expression or pose. A text description alone leaves a lot of room for the design to drift.

For the overall art style, choose a few reference images that work together and use them consistently for characters and backgrounds. Remember to describe the lighting, palette, and level of detail and being the more specific the better.

I’d also generate characters and backgrounds separately so you can reuse them across scenes. 

There’s still a fair amount of selecting, correcting, and editing involved but compared to months ago the frontier models now have been relatively consistent.

replies.author: zephyrion_drakon
replies.body: It depends on what tools you're using. I like Midjourney. It has capabilities for text input and using an input image so you can say "make this character do X with Y background, etc". It's also really, really good with matching styles. Much better than GPT Image imo which always gives you its own generic style, or you have to really fight it to get it to not do its own style tells. Midjourney has a dedicated input slot for style references.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body:
ask ai.  
  
like for real , make character sheets which give different angles of the characters , and make expression sheets with labels. so Happy-1 , very-happy-2,kinda-sad-5,sultry-5etc . How it works lets say he chars name is linda, you now say give me linda sitting on a bed with a sultry look , use sultry-02 from the expressions-sheet-1 file i attached as well as the linda char reference file . 

You also need to be paying close to top dollar for consistency , api calls are cheaper than some plan like higgsfield , and more advanced u can host image models on vast.ai. 

First thing u do is lock down the style by using a frontier model to describe the style u want , this is done by analyzing a few images it then gets u a prompt. Start a new chat with that prompt generate images and see if it matches

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
I never made a visual novel but to keep consistent character models I just always use a reference photo with all the angles of a character. (Character sheet). Also, you might want to make an expression set too. I'll show you one of mine:

https://preview.redd.it/9pj05b2hxfwh1.jpeg?width=1280&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=1c6873199f4017ba80e9e32ab85b796deefaa57a

replies.author: Entropydemic
replies.body: I think you might be able to even use the expression sheet here as a reference for another expression sheet.

comments.author: toiletman74
comments.body:
I only ever do local art gen so this is only relevant to local.

If the character is relatively simple in design you can use a reference image to image model like flux klein, just inputting a reference image of the character and telling it what you want the character to do.

If your character is more complex you're gonna be better off creating a lora of the character to get consistency.

comments.author: olafthemanofsnow
comments.body:
It comes down to a combination of tools for me.

Midjourney with style references and character images are my starting point. But midjourney doesnt handle text very well in images and will use loads of gibberish. So i would usually tidy it up in chatGPT for one off modifications. If you use the same image in chatgpt for multiple prompts you will start to encounter drift
